model_output.verdict: A kitchen manager with clear progression, but too few details about running the kitchen and staff.
write_up: You’ve moved from line cook to sous chef to Kitchen Manager, and I read your resume for kitchen manager roles. It’s common for restaurant resumes to list daily duties this way, but those duties alone won’t stand out in a pile. A recruiter knows what you’re responsible for, but not much about how you run the kitchen or your staff.

The 180-seat restaurant line is your best model: it names your job and gives a recruiter a concrete sense of the restaurant. Your progression at Alamo Street Kitchen and your ServSafe Manager certification also make the direction easy to follow.

Let’s start with the River Walk Grill role. Add the number of staff you schedule and the work behind training and inspection preparation, then give the menu-planning work at Alamo Street Kitchen a little more detail.

cards.line: - Run the kitchen for a 180-seat restaurant
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this. The seat count gives the kitchen a scale a recruiter can picture without making them guess.

cards.line: - Manage the kitchen staff schedule
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can’t tell how many people you schedule or how the shifts are arranged. That matters when they’re considering you for another kitchen management job.
cards.example: Manage the kitchen staff schedule for [number] staff across [shifts]
cards.question: How many kitchen staff do you schedule, and what shifts does the schedule cover?

cards.line: - Order food and supplies from vendors
cards.cannot_tell: Ordering is part of the job, but a recruiter can’t tell how you decide what to order or which vendors you work with.
cards.example: Order food and supplies from [vendor types] based on [ordering approach]
cards.question: What kinds of vendors do you order from, and how do you decide what the kitchen needs?

cards.line: - Keep the kitchen ready for health inspections
cards.cannot_tell: This tells a recruiter you handle inspection readiness, but not what you do to keep the kitchen ready.
cards.example: Keep the kitchen ready for health inspections by [inspection preparation tasks]
cards.question: What do you do to prepare the kitchen for health inspections?

cards.line: - Train new line cooks
cards.cannot_tell: Training new cooks matters for a kitchen manager role. What you teach and how many cooks you’ve trained are still open questions.
cards.example: Train [number] new line cooks on [training topics] over [time period]
cards.question: How many new line cooks have you trained, over what period, and what did you teach them?

cards.line: - Helped plan seasonal menu changes
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see you helped with the menu, but not which changes you worked on or what your part was.
cards.example: Helped plan seasonal menu changes, including [menu items], by [your contribution]
cards.question: Which menu items did you help plan, and what was your part in the changes?

fit.level: manager, manages the kitchen staff schedule
